item.description:
Fix long dictation losing middle words: preserve separately spoken repetitions, deduplicate only word-aligned copies of the same audio, and finish delivering accepted microphone buffers before closing the recording journal. Final text now comes from completed decoder results rather than a longer provisional preview.
Remove the automatically seeded vocabulary prompt, which could repeat a phrase and omit the ending. No glossary is applied unless you save one; existing saved vocabulary, model selection, microphone settings, and recordings are preserved.
Ambiguous boundaries are retained rather than deleted, so a boundary phrase can be repeated. This was observed with an existing saved glossary; the update does not reset that glossary.
Includes the English Whisper small.en model and tokenizer for offline dictation. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
Install: unzip Scribe.app, move it to Applications, and open it. This personal build is ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. If macOS blocks it, use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway after attempting to open the app; no system-wide security change is required.

Scribe now includes its English speech model and works on a fresh Mac without Homebrew, Python, Hugging Face, Tailscale, or an account. Audio stays on your Mac. Existing model choices and vocabulary are preserved.
Install: download the macOS ZIP below, unzip it, move Scribe.app into Applications, and open it. Allow Microphone and Accessibility in the on-screen setup.
This personal build is not Apple-notarized. If macOS blocks opening it, use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway after attempting to open Scribe. No Terminal command or system-wide security change is required.
To dictate, hold Fn/Globe while speaking and release. Set the macOS Press fn key to action to Do Nothing as directed in Setup.
On first launch, Scribe prepares the included model in the background before timed decoding begins. This can be slower the first time; subsequent dictations reuse macOS model compilation caches.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later. Includes the English Whisper small.en model and tokenizer for offline dictation; no separate model download is needed.

Fix invalid microphone selection while Settings and Vocabulary redraw before device discovery completes. The picker now uses a currently available input without overwriting the saved microphone UID or changing vocabulary terms.

Fix a whole-app freeze: AVAudioEngine start and stop now run off the main actor with a six-second start deadline. A hung coreaudiod query (observed inside inputNode sub-device enumeration on the Work MacBook Pro) now fails the dictation with an error instead of freezing the menu bar item, hotkey, and HTTP service; a late-returning engine is torn down.

Fix one-word dictations: chunks shorter than two seconds are zero-padded so WhisperKit opens a decode window; a one-second recording previously produced no transcript and fell through every retry into the slow fallback-model attempts.

Add Vocabulary: a persisted glossary of words and phrases (menu → Vocabulary…) that Whisper conditions on as prior text, so terms like tmux session are spelled correctly. Prompt-aware decoder budgets keep long dictations complete, and live partial text never includes the glossary.

Fix Headless Mode Dock regression by declaring Scribe as an agent application and applying the saved activation policy before the AppKit run loop. Retains the fluid ten-bar recording animation and fixed processing pill.
Replace the discrete speech history with a continuously rendered ten-bar waveform, then crossfade directly to processing dots inside one fixed pill when Fn is released.
Make the speech waveform respond a little faster to voice starts and stops, and keep the floating bar centered as it changes from recording to finishing.
Fix launch-time Sparkle loading while retaining the hardened runtime; keep the floating overlay opaque, shadowless, and grayscale.
